title: Made By
logline: Over twenty-one months a Minecraft map maker teaches machines to help him make PvP maps for his community, from a spanning tree drawn in redstone to boards that staff take for touched-up work, and ends with a map he built by hand that players take for AI.
narration: One narrator: plain, dry, third person, past tense for events and present tense for the recording. Beside it only voices of the record: the 2 July recording where cleared, and rockymine's own written messages read by himself (scratch voice until then). Other people's written words appear on screen as text, never voiced.

acts.title: A spanning tree in redstone
acts.summary: February 2025 to May 2026, before the studio: the algorithm written to samschaap, the answer that it would be rules and not training, tools from v0, Claude, Gemini and his own C# editor, a winter of logged matches, the islands that turned back into a graph, and the stowaways that drawing every map turned up.

acts.title: Just having Claude follow along
acts.summary: October and November 2026: agents fail to compose his mountain sketch, he builds the map by hand, the agents are put to reading it, players ask whether it is AI, the freeform boards finally reach the public servers, and the studio stands in the browser.

scenes.title: Every check passed
scenes.picture: Animated: the Prompt-a-Map machine presents a version of the mountain map on a plinth; a ramp on it runs off into the void and a character walks off it. Stamp: REJECTED, then the next version.

frame.sketch: a ramp running off into the void, stamped REJECTED

scenes.vo: NARRATOR: In November agents were asked to compose a sketch of his, a map set into a mountain. Every version was rejected. The surface was not closed. A ramp led into the void. Every one of those failures passed some check that existed at the time.

onscreen.text: Every one of those failures passed some check that existed at the time
a ramp led into the void

scenes.title: The map he built
scenes.picture: The hand-built half: whole from above, then a slow descent into the valley and along the routes, one render per route.

frame.sketch: the hand-built half from above: cauldron of walls, bunker facade

scenes.vo: NARRATOR: He had begun building it himself in the middle of October, over a few weekends. A bunker set into a mountain, the core in its face, a wool lane underground. Tunnels, a lane, a way over the top, a hole from the floor into the lane, a door high in the facade. The agents' task became reading it.

onscreen.text: a CTW and DTC hybrid for a fire-and-ice contest

scenes.sound: Wind, then the inside of a tunnel.

scenes.picture: Render of the wool lookout from the valley; the study's labels for spaces appear and fade, too many to read.

frame.sketch: the wool lookout seen from the valley floor

scenes.vo: NARRATOR: The agents' study names forty-two spaces in it. The studio's own dead-ground rule would refuse it. The study comes to one line.

onscreen.text: a geometric rule is not a design

scenes.title: Still not AI
scenes.picture: Render of the facade and core; his message appears in a chat bubble at the bottom of the frame.

frame.sketch: the bunker facade with the core set in it

scenes.vo: NARRATOR: On the twenty-fifth of November he sent its layers to a map developer, with a note. ROCKYMINE (his message, read): Note that it still is not AI. Just having claude follow along.

onscreen.text: Note that it still is not AI. Just having claude follow along.

scenes.title: Is it AI?
scenes.picture: The author's own gameplay on the hand-built map, players running the underground lane. Tag: author recalls.

frame.sketch: inside the underground wool lane

scenes.vo: NARRATOR: Players ask him, it feels constantly, whether what he builds is AI. A player asked it first of this map. He finds it funny. He says it looked a little wild at the start, and a model's work is not wild. It is more structured.

scenes.vo: NARRATOR: The studio is a website now, pgmstudio.de, on a small machine he rents. Anyone can draw a map in it. He hid the model-made maps there, because they might give a wrong impression. He says hardly anyone uses it.

scenes.title: What belongs
scenes.picture: rockymine and Ruediger, their real skins, stand on the hand-built map's floor; the camera rises over the walls to the whole half.

scenes.vo: NARRATOR: What the tools have not taken over is the judgement of what a place is for. The rules can say that ground lies off every route. They cannot say what belongs.
